367:     fn process(&self) {
368:         // Check if the pipe is ready to read and therefore has "woken" us up
369:         //
370:         // To do so, we will `poll_read_ready` with a noop waker, since we don't
371:         // need to actually be notified when read ready...
372:         let waker = unsafe { Waker::from_raw(RawWaker::new(ptr::null(), &NOOP_WAKER_VTABLE)) };
373:         let mut cx = Context::from_waker(&waker);
374: 
375:         let ev = match self.receiver.registration().poll_read_ready(&mut cx) {
376:             Poll::Ready(Ok(ev)) => ev,
377:             Poll::Ready(Err(e)) => panic!("reactor gone: {}", e),
378:             Poll::Pending => return, // No wake has arrived, bail
379:         };
380: 
381:         // Drain the pipe completely so we can receive a new readiness event
382:         // if another signal has come in.
383:         let mut buf = [0; 128];
384:         loop {
385:             match (&*self.receiver).read(&mut buf) {
386:                 Ok(0) => panic!("EOF on self-pipe"),
387:                 Ok(_) => continue, // Keep reading
388:                 Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
389:                 Err(e) => panic!("Bad read on self-pipe: {}", e),
390:             }
391:         }
392: 
393:         self.receiver.registration().clear_readiness(ev);
394: 
395:         // Broadcast any signals which were received
396:         globals().broadcast();
397:     }
398: }

part.text:
Fixed. The signal driver's self-pipe was registered with `Interest::READABLE | Interest::WRITABLE` even though nothing ever writes to it, causing a busy-spin with level-triggered selectors. The fix in tokio/src/signal/unix/driver.rs:

- `watch_writable` changed to `false` (line 75)
- Registration now uses `Interest::READABLE` only (line 348)

All signal tests (`signal_ctrl_c`, `signal_drop_recv`, `signal_multi_rt`, `signal_usr1`, etc.) plus runtime and io-driver tests pass.
